prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Mixed · Multilingual glossary (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "English" · longest unbreakable word 67px · one-line width 146px
  col 2: header "中文" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 54px
  col 3: header "日本語" · longest unbreakable word 14px · one-line width 93px
  col 4: header "한국어" · longest unbreakable word 12px · one-line width 64px
  col 5: header "العربية" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 97px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 480px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 479px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Provide equivalent glossary terms across five languages.","reading":"Readers find a term in one language and scan across its row to compare translations; consistent row alignment helps them keep their place.","groups":["All five columns serve the same role as language equivalents; English can also act as an entry point for readers of this English-language table.","Chinese, Japanese, and Korean terms are compact and can share the middle of the table without requiring identical widths."],"keep_intact":["Individual English and Arabic words and all language names.","Short glossary terms where space permits, especially compact Chinese, Japanese, and Korean entries."],"may_wrap":["Multiword English and Arabic terms can wrap between words.","Longer Japanese and Korean terms may wrap at natural script-appropriate boundaries; wrapping can share row height with translations that already need multiple lines."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [125, 75, 105, 85, 89] · table 480×240px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [115, 75, 114, 85, 90] · table 480×240px · row heights [33, 33, 33, 33, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [135, 75, 100, 85, 84] · table 480×280px · row heights [33, 33, 53, 53, 53, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
